proposal.description: The cycle boundary is taken on the rising edge of the PWM instead of the falling edge, so the ceiling steps at the start of a pulse rather than after it.
proposal.reason: In S_SS, max_on_counts now changes on the clock after pwm_sync rises, while the pulse is still on, instead of after it falls. Each step lands earlier by the width of the PWM pulse, and so does SS_done.

before: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
proposal.description: A max_on_limit lowered during S_RUN is clamped onto the held ceiling straight away, instead of being left until the next ramp.
proposal.reason: If the host lowers max_on_limit while run_active is high, max_on_counts drops to the new limit on the next clock. The header says the ceiling stays unchanged through S_RUN and the new limit only takes effect at the next soft start.

proposal.description: The ceiling steps on the first switching cycle of each step window instead of its last.
proposal.reason: On entering S_SS with cycles_per_step > 1, max_on_counts rises at the very first PWM falling edge, not after cycles_per_step cycles. The whole ramp, and SS_done, therefore arrive cycles_per_step-1 switching cycles early.

before: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
proposal.description: SS_done is cleared on entry to S_RUN rather than held for all of S_RUN.
proposal.reason: After a completed ramp, SS_done falls on the first clock that run_active is high and stays low through S_RUN. The original holds it high until the supervisor leaves S_RUN.

proposal.description: The look-ahead meant only for SS_done is also used in the target test, so the last step lands as soon as the ceiling is one below the limit, without waiting out its step window.
proposal.reason: In S_SS, as soon as max_on_counts reaches max_on_limit-1, it jumps to max_on_limit and SS_done rises on the next clock. That can happen mid-pulse, and it skips the cycles_per_step-cycle dwell, so the ramp ends one step period early.

proposal.description: The edge detector's delayed PWM copy is only updated in S_SS, so it holds a stale value from the previous soft start.
proposal.reason: Suppose S_SS is left while pwm_sync is high (a hiccup, say), and a later S_SS begins with pwm_sync low. The stale pwm_sync_d=1 then makes a false falling edge on the first clock. That counts a switching cycle that never happened, so the first ceiling step comes one cycle early.
